source_section: Data Type Warnings and SQL Dialect Notes
summary: OMS amount columns are strings requiring CAST/TRY_CAST; financial settlement/reverse columns are doubles; date parsing uses Trino/Athena functions.
The DOCX lists gross commission, commission rate/discount, MP fees, pick-pack, payment gateway fee, fixed fee, freight, reverse, marketing, royalty, and forward additional charges.
Settlement, reverse, and non-order settlement require is_active=true; OMS has no is_active column; group_level_id is a table column/filter caveat.

The DOCX explicitly defines forward sale and reverse return/refund operational lifecycles with source table references; non-order transactions are documented as financial entries not tied to orders, not as a separate ordered lifecycle.
Applied evidence anchoring, card-type fit, process-vs-reconciliation, process-variant discipline, SQL-ref integrity, scope-identifier, and review-state discipline manifests.
Myntra is an Indian fashion marketplace using an MP model where sellers own inventory and Myntra earns marketplace commissions and fees.

Myntra splits each fee, commission, settlement component, UTR reference, and settlement date into prepaid and postpaid/COD streams; this is a value/query stream split, not a process variant by itself.
The DOCX provides SQL for forward orders, OMS gross sales, net settlement, return rate, and pending receivables by aging.
The DOCX defines Level 1 OMS-to-settlement reconciliation through myntra_oms_settlement: sales_amount (OMS) equals sales_settled_amount (Settlement), with recon_status values.
The DOCX provides an entity map from OMS to settlement, reverse, seller reports, expenses, and receivables; non-order settlement does not join to OMS/reverse.
The DOCX says all tables should be scoped by group_level_id; the concrete client value is runtime context and must not create tenant/group/account-binding cards.
The DOCX provides detailed schemas for myntra_oms, myntra_settlement, myntra_reverse, and myntra_non_order_settlement.
GST, TCS, and TDS are marketplace deduction columns/metrics, not statutory filing cards.
transaction_type supports forward/reverse, internal_txn_type supports sales/reverse/NULL, and reverse order_status supports cancelled/NULL.
